title: Wheel Spinner — Spin a Free Name Wheel Online
description: A free wheel spinner that runs in your browser: paste names, spin, and get one winner with its chance shown. No sign-up, nothing uploaded.
h1: Wheel Spinner: spin a list and get one winner
heroText: A wheel spinner turns a list of names into a spinning wheel and stops on one at random. This one runs in your browser: paste your names, spin, and the wheel lands on a single winner. The draw is made before the wheel moves, with the browser's secure random numbers, so the spin only shows a pick that was already fair. No sign-up, and your names are not uploaded.

ctas.label: See how the winner is drawn

sections.title: What a wheel spinner does
sections.body: The wheel is a fair way to pick from a list without anyone deciding. You paste the entries, they become equal slices, and one slice is chosen at random when you spin.

items.title: Before the wheel turns
items.body: The winner is drawn first, using crypto.getRandomValues and rejection sampling, so an even spin cannot hide an uneven chance. The animation then settles on that slice.

items.title: What you see at the end
items.body: A result card with the winner, that entry's chance in the draw and how many entries are left. A wheel of six names gives each one a 1-in-6 chance, shown as about 16.7%.

items.title: Same tool, other jobs
items.body: Weighted entries, several winners in order and a randomness check are the [picker wheel](/picker-wheel/), the [raffle wheel](/raffle-wheel/) and the fairness page. This page is the plain spin.

sections.title: Spin a name wheel in four steps
sections.body: A first spin takes about as long as typing your list.

items.title: A worked example: club raffle
items.body: Forty entrants go into the box, one per line. Each slice carries 2.5%, and the card reports that chance beside the winner's name. Call the name out once the wheel stops, then remove it so the second prize cannot repeat the first.

steps.title: Paste your list
steps.body: One name per line in the text box. A class register, a team rota or the entrants in a giveaway all work as a pasted column.

steps.title: Check the slices
steps.body: Every name gets its own slice with its percentage chance printed on it, so a duplicated line is easy to spot before you spin.

steps.title: Spin
steps.body: Press the spin button. The wheel turns five to seven seconds, then slows onto the slice already drawn.

steps.title: Read the result
steps.body: The card names the winner. Spin again, or [remove the winner](/picker-wheel/) from the list so the next spin picks someone else.

sections.title: Where this wheel spinner stops
sections.body: Knowing the edges saves a surprise in the middle of an event.

items.title: No images on slices
items.body: Entries are text. The wheel draws names, teams, numbers or short answers, not pictures or logos.

items.title: No saved wheel on the free tier
items.body: The free tier loads the wheel in your browser and keeps no library of named wheels between sessions. Saving wheels, keeping a draw history and syncing devices are what [Plus](/pricing/) adds.

items.title: It stays in the browser
items.body: Nothing is sent anywhere, which also means another device cannot join the same spin. That is why synced devices start on Plus.

items.title: One wheel at a time
items.body: The page spins one list, one result at a time. Drawing several winners in a set order is the [raffle wheel](/raffle-wheel/), and a weighted list goes to the [picker wheel](/picker-wheel/).

items.title: Bring your own list
items.body: There is no database of names to search. Every draw starts from the lines you paste, so a mislabelled entry shows up on a slice exactly as you typed it.

faq.question: Is this wheel spinner free?
faq.answer: Yes. Pasting names, spinning and reading the result cost nothing and need no account. The free tier runs the wheel in the browser.

faq.question: Can the result be predicted from the list order?
faq.answer: No. The winner is drawn from the whole list with the browser's secure random numbers, not from where a slice sits, so moving names around does not change any entry's chance. The [fairness page](/fairness/) explains the method and lets you run 10,000 draws yourself.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: Once the page has loaded, the spin and the draw run on your device with no network call, so a dropped connection does not disturb a spin already in progress. Loading the page for the first time still needs a connection.

faq.question: How many names can I paste?
faq.answer: You can paste a long class list or raffle sheet. Past a few dozen names the labels on the slices shrink, so the result card is the reliable place to read the winner and its chance.

faq.question: What happens to my names after I close the page?
faq.answer: They stay on your device as the wheel's last list and are not uploaded to a server. There is nothing to sign in for: names stay in this browser tab and no entry text is sent anywhere.
